usage.notes: Use NIH 3D as a discovery/acquisition source. Panacea should ingest only explicitly selected entries after per-entry provenance, version, citation and license checks. Production runtime should serve Panacea-controlled optimized derivatives rather than hot-linking portal assets.

license.scope: NIH 3D Terms state that licensing is assigned by contributors and varies by entry/file. Many entries are public domain or Creative Commons, while others may have more restrictive terms. No portal-wide commercial-use permission may be inferred for individual models.
license.notes: Block asset ingestion when the specific NIH 3D entry does not have a recorded license, attribution instruction, stable entry identifier and version. Store those fields on every derived Panacea asset manifest.

validation.notes: NIH 3D is a biomedical visualization repository with heterogeneous contributor content. Individual models may be useful for education or reference but must not be treated as patient-specific anatomy, diagnostic evidence or validated procedural guidance without separate validation.

provenance.authority: NIH 3D, U.S. National Institutes of Health biomedical 3D model portal
provenance.notes: Record the NIH 3D accession/PID, entry version, creator, source-data attribution, citation instructions, original license and every Panacea transformation. Source authority does not erase contributor-level provenance requirements.

adapter.notes: Planned pipeline: select NIH 3D entry -> verify entry metadata/license -> acquire supported file -> normalize anatomical identity -> mesh cleanup/LOD/compression -> derived GLB/glTF -> Panacea anatomy renderer.
